previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis was admitted after vomiting coffee-ground material, concerning for upper gastrointestinal bleeding. She had a history of esophageal varices and presented with a low-grade fever and mild hypoxemia. An EGD revealed high-risk stigmata on grade II varices, which were successfully banded. She remained hemodynamically stable throughout her stay, with no further bleeding. The fever resolved without a clear infectious source, and hypoxemia improved, attributed to atelectasis rather than hepatopulmonary syndrome, as confirmed by a normal bubble echocardiogram. She completed a course of prophylactic ceftriaxone for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and was started on sucralfate for mucosal healing. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all home medications, complete a 14-day course of sucralfate, and follow up for a repeat endoscopy in four weeks.
